newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia sees 3.5 pct 1997 GDP if reforms pursued.
newsitem.headline: Latvia sees 3.5 pct 1997 GDP if reforms pursued.

text.p: The Latvian economy ministry on Tuesday forecast 3.5 percent gross domestic product (GDP) growth for 1997 and five to six percent growth in 1998 if active reform policies are maintained and investment levels are high.
But the report warned GDP could be lower if competition in the key transit business increased and investments were low.
Latvia has got back on the growth path after suffering from a banking crisis in 1995 that led to a 1.6 percent fall in GDP.
Last year the economy stabilised and 1996 growth is expected to be 2.5 percent, after 2.3 percent growth for nine months.
"Our forecasts show that if active economic reform policies are continued, it is possible that from 1998 GDP can grow by at least five to six percent a year," the report said.
But it noted that the GDP growth of 1996 did not mean the whole economy had stabilised, as much of the growth was due to more active business in transport and oil transit.
Latvia's Ventspils oil terminal is one of the main outlets for Russian crude oil and the country as a whole likes to portray itself as a bridge between Russia and the West.
The report said transit activities during the first nine months of 1996 rose 15.1 percent compared to the same period last year but retail trade fell and incomes were not growing.

The ministry prepared two separate forecasts for future GDP growth. The optimistic view predicted growth of between five and six percent in 1998 if investments and exports rise and the more pessimistic view saw two to three percent growth if investment is low and competition in the transit business gets tougher.
